Lessons.Title: Compare Perimeters of Rectangles
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will apply multiplicative reasoning and your knowledge of fractions to solve problems about perimeters of rectangles.
Represent both quantities, compare their values, and state the relationship using words, symbols, or a clear explanation.
Core relationship: Perimeters of rectangles. Perimeter is twice the sum of length and width; compare perimeters rather than area.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up: Number Talk: Two and Four Times a Fraction	 (10 minutes); Activity 1: Pipe-cleaner Perimeters (10 minutes); Activity 2: Perimeter Predictions	 (15 minutes); Activity 3:  Gridded Rectangles	 (10 minutes); Cool-down:  Rectangles Y and Z	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: A rectangle is 8 cm by 5 cm. Find its perimeter.
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): Find the perimeter of a 9 cm by 4 cm rectangle.
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

KeyConcepts.Title: Exact source-goal relationship
KeyConcepts.Definition: The perimeter of a rectangle is twice its length plus twice its width.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Multiplying length by width gives area, not perimeter.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Perimeter is twice the sum of length and width; compare perimeters rather than area.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using area instead of perimeter when comparing boundaries.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The reasoning does not preserve the task's mathematical quantities or representation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Perimeter adds all four sides, not length×width.
